newsitem.title: USA: Temple-Inland sees container prices rising.
newsitem.headline: Temple-Inland sees container prices rising.

text.p: Temple-Inland Inc today said it expects to see an improvement in pricing for its corrugated containers during the third quarters and "solid" results for its building products and financial services group for the rest of the year.

"We continue to be encouraged by the strength of demand for our corrugated containers, and we anticipate an improvement in pricing for this product during the third quarter," said Clifford Grum, Temple-Inland's chairman and chief executive officer, in a statement.

Earlier, the company reported second quarter net income of $15.6 million, or $0.28 per share, with the building products group and financial services group both posting record quarterly operating earnings, the company said.
According to First Call, analysts had estimated Temple-Inland's second quarter earnings at $0.23 per share.
The paper group recorded an operating loss of $10.1 million in the second quarter. This compares with operating earnings for the group of $28.8 million a year ago.
Prices for boxes dropped early in the quarter before stabilizing late in the quarter, more than offsetting the benefit of record volumes.
Average box prices in the quarter were down $108 per ton from last year's second quarter, the company said.
